title: What an accompanist does for a singer
summary: Asked about Billie, Ella and Sarah, he says to listen to the singer, and praises Shearing.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them

blocks.x: Let's talk a little bit about singers.
All right. I can always talk about singers.
You have accompanied the greatest, and especially what people would think of as the three great ladies -- Billie, Ella and Sarah. What can an accompanist do for a singer, and how does he do it?
Well, the first thing you do is listen to her

sing. Hear how she sings. Then you try to play to make her happy. You don't play too much, you don't play enough, this, that, you know... And of course, all singers are crazy. Like George Shearing says, what's that famous thing he said...? "There are four sexes, male, female, homosexual and girl singers." And I think he said it right.
Incidentally, speaking of George Shearing, I think he is probably one of the finest solo pianists I have ever heard in my life. I admire George Shearing very much, and I like him personally.
